# Summary of Police Complaint in Texas Lieutenant Governor Race

**Who Filed and When:**
State Rep. Vikki Goodwin, the Democratic candidate for lieutenant governor, filed a police report with the Travis County Sheriff's Office on Saturday, September 19, 2026.

**What Was Filed:**
Goodwin submitted a sworn affidavit accusing Republican Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick of violating Texas law after his campaign released two AI-generated videos depicting her.

**Affidavit Language:**
Goodwin stated: "I did not personally do or say the things depicted in the video; although the 'person' in the video appears to be me, it was not actually me." She also declared that Patrick "posted the video with the intent to deceive Texans, injure a candidate, or influence the result."

**The 2019 Texas Law:**
Goodwin cited legislation banning deepfake videos from publication or distribution within 30 days of an election. The statute defines such videos as appearing to depict a real person performing actions that didn't occur, with intent to deceive.

**Early Voting Date:**
In-person early voting begins October 19, 2026.

**Patrick Campaign's Response:**
Allen Blakemore, Patrick's campaign spokesman, told the New York Times the material was "an obvious parody produced to entertain" and that "no reasonable person could view it any other way." He added they had not distributed these materials within the 30-day window.

**Timeline Note:**
The videos were deleted from Patrick's X account the day after Goodwin filed her complaint.

Q1 2027 is roughly three to six months after the 2026-09-22 edition date; "a year and a bit" is the script's own invention and overstates the delay. The follow-on line compounds it: Script (host A): "A year and a bit is a long time in this market." — no edition text supports any duration characterisation.

**2. Bessent — "yesterday" converted to "Sunday"**
Script (item "Bessent says the US and China have formalised…", host A): "He also said the talks ran about 12 hours on Sunday."
Edition: "Bessent said the talks with the Chinese vice premier ran \"about 12 hours yesterday\", covering economics and AI".
The edition never names a day; "Sunday" is a derived date. The counterparty ("the Chinese vice premier") is also dropped.

**3. Intro — Texas caveat dropped**
Script (intro, host B): "Texas ordered its environmental regulator to stop issuing data centre permits, and California's governor signed seven data centre laws."
Edition summary: "Texas Governor Greg Abbott ordered the state environmental regulator to issue no data-centre permits until grid and water audits are complete".
The conditional "until grid and water audits are complete" — the limit that makes it a pause rather than a ban — is missing. (The later item block does include it; the intro does not.)

**4. RRSI paper — scope of the 14.1-point gain changed**
Script (item "Google Cloud AI Research reports constrained recursive self-improvement…", host B): "reports gains of up to 14.1 points on the benchmarks it trains against."
Edition: "RRSI \"gains up to 14.1 points on the split it evolves against…\"" and "The backbone model is frozen — only the harness evolves."
Singular "the split" becomes plural "the benchmarks", and "evolves against" becomes "trains against" — which also cuts against the edition's own point that no training occurs.

**5. RRSI paper — attribution characterised as one lab**
Script (host A): "the results are a company claim from the lab that wrote it."
Edition: "the results are the authors' own" / "Author affiliations listed on the arXiv HTML are Google Cloud AI Research, Stanford University, Washington University in St. Louis and UNC-Chapel Hill."
Four affiliations, three of them universities; "the lab that wrote it" is a characterisation the edition does not make.

**6. Unsupported same-day link for the math story**
Script (item "OpenAI publishes frontier-safety proposals…", host B): "The same day, OpenAI published a set of frontier-safety proposals."
Edition: summary says only "Separately on Monday the company published frontier-safety proposals"; the maths item gives no announcement date, only "OpenAI dated the start of that model's training to August 28."
The edition makes a same-day comparison for Alibaba vs OpenAI, not for the maths claim vs the safety post.

**7. Bessent quote — dropped attribution frame**
Script (item "Bessent says the Hugging Face incident…", host B): "Bessent said it is humans who are responsible, not the AI…"
Edition: "\"I am in agreement with the MIT professor who leads the AI lab up there, Daniel Huttenlocher, that it is humans who are responsible, not the AI…\""
Bessent's framing as agreement with a named third party is removed and the view presented as his own assertion.

**8. Border towers — cost estimate loses its date**
Script (item "MIT Technology Review maps more than 1,050 migrant deaths…", host B): "with a government estimate of $6.2 billion over their lifespan"
Edition: "in 2023 the government estimated its plans for the towers, \"which now number 803, would cost $6.2 billion over their lifespan\""
"in 2023" — a three-year-old estimate — is dropped.

**9. Alibaba self-improvement — tool calls generalised**
Script (item "Alibaba says Qwen3.8-Max ran 33 automated self-improvement cycles…", host A): "made more than 10,000 tool calls"
Edition: "making more than 10,000 EDA tool calls to produce production-grade chip bus modules"
"EDA" dropped, broadening a chip-design-specific figure into generic tool use.

**10. Grok pricing — tier dropped**
Script (item "xAI releases Grok 4.7…", host A): "xAI put out Grok 4.7 at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens"
Edition: "xAI's launch page lists Grok 4.7 xHigh at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens"
The price is for the "xHigh" configuration, not Grok 4.7 generally.

**11. Zhenwu V900 — caveat over-broadened**
Script (host B): "All of that is a company claim, unverified, and no benchmark results against Nvidia parts were published."
Edition: "The performance multiple, memory and bandwidth figures are Alibaba's own and unverified; no benchmark results against Nvidia parts were published."
"All of that" sweeps in the CEO's 20GW quote and the 500,000-card claim, which the edition scopes differently.

**12. Minor wording changes to characterisations**
- Script (EAGLE item, host A): "from ordinary chest CT scans" vs edition "from chest noncontrast CT" — "ordinary" is the script's gloss.
- Script (political audit item, host A): "shows the behaviour changing between versions in a way current audits miss" vs edition's quoted "shows the regime changing between versions in a way current audits miss."
